application_guidance.input_pattern: Linear root finding with pre-update averaging and a slowly decreasing power-law gain.
read_original_when: Changing drift, output, gain schedule or noise conditions.
Using Appendix algebra or estimates as independently certified proof steps.
sensitive_conditions: Positive real parts of every eigenvalue of A.
Deterministic x_0, power exponent strictly between zero and one.
All conditional martingale, moment, tail and covariance hypotheses in the statement.

complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Limit covariance is A^(-1) S A^(-T); no uniform convergence rate, burn-in or finite-time constants supplied.
complexity_scope.oracle: One residual y_t=A x_(t-1)-b+xi_t at each history-dependent iterate, under the stated noise assumptions.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Pre-update arithmetic average; weak limit of sqrt(t)(bar x_t-x*).
complexity_scope.regime: Fixed d,A,b,x_0,c,a and qualifying noise law as t->infinity.
complexity_scope.resource: t noisy residual calls for t recursion steps; no finite-accuracy sample bound.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Selected Eq.(2) linear SA with power-law decreasing gain; no coverage of arbitrary estimators.

content.intended_use: Identify the limit law of the selected pre-update iterate average.

proofs.locator: Appendix printed844–848, Lemma1–2 and Proof of Theorem1 Part1, Eq.(A1)–(A10).
map: Lemma1 printed844–846 introduces transition and averaged matrices. In the decreasing-gain branch, establish t gamma_t ->infinity, eventual transition decay via a Lyapunov equation, and bounded averaged errors with vanishing Cesaro remainder using summation by parts.

Lemma2 printed846–847 expands the recursion into an initialization term, an A^(-1)-weighted martingale sum and a weighted noise remainder; weights are uniformly bounded and their Cesaro norm vanishes.
Theorem1 Part1 printed847 uses these bounds to discard initialization and weighted remainder, displaying a mean-square estimate.
Printed847–848 invokes Assumption2.4 for Lindeberg and Assumption2.5(a) for conditional covariance convergence, then cites its bibliography [17], Theorem5.5.11, for a martingale CLT.
proofs.omitted_details: Literature Proof map only. Lemma1–2 are internal source dependencies at the stated locators, not separate scientific records. Bibliography [17] was not independently read or extracted. No local transfer or independent reproof is claimed.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actually read Appendix notation, Lemma1 statement/decreasing-gain proof, Lemma2 statement/proof and Theorem1 Part1 through its conclusion using original-page JPEGs for PDF pp.7–11.

source_issues.reason: Printed Eq.(A9) and Lemma2 expansion use positive noise terms, whereas Eq.(2)/(A8) has negative noise. This map does not certify exact signed identities.
The source displays a deterministic-K mean-square estimate although Assumption2.3 gives an almost-sure conditional bound. An independent localization justification is not supplied here.

assumptions: Fixed A in R^(dxd), b in R^d, with Re lambda_i(A)>0 for every eigenvalue. Initial x_0 in R^d is arbitrary deterministic (Assumption2.1 and Eq.(2)).
gamma_t=c t^(-a), c>0 and 0<a<1. This selected subcase satisfies Eq.(4): gamma_t ->0 and (gamma_t-gamma_(t+1))/gamma_t=o(gamma_t).
On a probability space with increasing filtration F_t, xi_t is F_t-measurable, E[xi_t|F_(t-1)]=0 and sup_(t>=1) E[||xi_t||^2|F_(t-1)]<infinity almost surely (Assumption2.3).
Assumption2.4 as printed: lim_(C->infinity) limsup_(t->infinity) E[||xi_t||^2 1_{||xi_t||>C}|F_(t-1)]=0 in probability.
E[xi_t xi_t^T|F_(t-1)] -> S in probability for a deterministic symmetric positive definite matrix S (Assumption2.5(a)).
statement.conclusion: sqrt(t)(bar x_t-x*) converges in distribution to N(0,A^(-1) S A^(-T)).
statement.objects_and_definitions: For integer t>=1, x_t=x_(t-1)-gamma_t(A x_(t-1)-b+xi_t), bar x_t=(1/t) sum_(i=0)^(t-1)x_i and x*=A^(-1)b. Norm is Euclidean.
statement.parameter_domains: d is any finite positive integer; A,b fixed real matrix/vector; c>0; 0<a<1; S fixed symmetric positive definite.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed finite-dimensional system, deterministic initialization, c>0, a in (0,1), probability space, filtration and noise process satisfying all listed assumptions, the distributional conclusion holds as integer t->infinity.
